name: Tolperisone + Etoricoxib
meta: Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Centrally acting muscle relaxant (non-sedating); Etoricoxib: Selective COX-2 inhibitor (NSAID)
Schedule H – prescription only; Etoricoxib: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.
White to off-white powder, slightly soluble in water.

Tolperisone Hydrochloride: In use since the 1960s; after a 2012 EMA referral, use in the EU was restricted to adults with post-stroke spasticity because of hypersensitivity reactions. First approval/introduction: Developed in Hungary in the 1960s (Gedeon Richter).

Etoricoxib: The MEDAL programme (34,701 patients) showed thrombotic cardiovascular event rates comparable to diclofenac with fewer upper GI events. First approval/introduction: Patented 1996; approved 2002 (Merck & Co.) – approved in >80 countries, not in the USA.
Combines COX-2 selective analgesia (better GI tolerance) with a non-sedating centrally acting muscle relaxant.

Tolperisone Hydrochloride Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes; relieves muscle spasm and spasticity without significant sedation. Receptor / target profile: Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes without sedation.

Etoricoxib Highly selective inhibitor of cyclo-oxygenase-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis at sites of inflammation while largely sparing COX-1-mediated gastric protection and platelet function. Receptor / target profile: Highly selective COX-2 inhibitor (~106-fold COX-2 over COX-1 in human whole-blood assays).
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 0.5–1 h (ER prolongs); high first-pass metabolism (CYP2D6, CYP2C19). Half-life ~2.5 h.
Summary: Bioavailability ~100%; Tmax ~1 h. ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life ~22 h (once-daily dosing).

Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Take after meals with water (food increases bioavailability).
Etoricoxib: With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Etoricoxib: BP within 2 weeks of starting and periodically; renal function; LFTs.
Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Ataxia, hypotonia, seizures, dyspnoea. Supportive care. Etoricoxib: GI and renal effects, CV events possible. Supportive care; not dialysable.
